L403@P9: 7. Dataset Validation and Example Use
L404@P9: We validate that the dataset is internally consistent and immediately usable; deeper scientific
L405@P9: analysis is left to companion work.
L406@P9: Reproducibility.
L407@P9: A bundled harness recomputes headline statistics directly from the released CSV/JSON and
L408@P9: matches the stored values to ≤ 10−3 under a fixed random seed, confirming that the published
L409@P9: numbers are regenerable from the raw records alone.
L410@P9: Quantization Integrity.
L411@P9: Stage A quantization accuracy retention is reported directly in Section 3.1 (Table 1) to keep the
L412@P9: method-to-data flow linear. For the valid per-device subset used in cross-device examples, FP32 and
L413@P9: INT8 top-1 remain strongly rank-consistent (Pearson r ∈ [0.953, 0.963], n≈577), confirming that the
L414@P9: PTQ path preserves model identity rather than corrupting it.
L415@P9: Delegate-Resolved Structure.
L416@P9: Because each record carries per-delegate timings and a winner label, the dataset supports queries
L417@P9: that opaque single-number benchmarks cannot, e.g. winning-backend distribution shifts across tiers
L418@P9: and realised INT8 speedup per device (median 4.1× on Snapdragon 888 down to 1.6× on Kirin 710;
L419@P9: Table 10). These are reported here only to demonstrate that the released fields are populated and
L420@P9: queryable.
L421@P9: Table 10. Example descriptive queries answerable directly from the released records (per device). Reported to
L422@P9: illustrate dataset utility, not as scientific claims.

L429@P9: 8. Data Access, Hosting, Licensing, and Maintenance
L430@P9: The dataset is released in two complementary forms: (i) the per-run JSON records (one file per
L431@P9: device under FP32/INT8 directories) together with a merged CSV and a machine-readable cross-device
L432@P9: summary, and (ii) the converted TFLite model zoo (FP32 and INT8 binaries). The records use the schema
L433@P9: of Table 4; a data dictionary documents every column’s unit and meaning. The dataset and the model
L434@P9: zoo are distributed under a permissive license for research use, while the conversion/benchmarking
L435@P9: code is released through the public nn-lite and nn-dataset repositories. A persistent identifier (DOI)
L436@P9: is provided for the data snapshot. The released bundle includes a minimal working example and a
L437@P9: reproduction harness that regenerates the headline statistics from the raw records, so the artefact is
L438@P9: self-verifying. Resource links are listed in the Data Availability Statement.
L439@P9: 9. Limitations
L440@P9: AI on the Edge measures wall-clock latency under a fixed protocol; it does not isolate DVFS
L441@P9: governor state or per-operator energy, and reported wall-clock includes deliberate thermal pauses
L442@P9: (we therefore separate raw measurement from total span). The fleet contains one device per tier, so
L443@P9: device telemetry is rich but cross-device generalisation is limited by sample size at the SoC level. The
L444@P9: Preprints.org (www.preprints.org) | NOT PEER-REVIEWED | Posted: 21 July 2026 doi:10.20944/preprints202511.1831.v2
L445@P9-10: © 2026 by the author(s). Distributed under a Creative Commons CC BY license.10 of 12
L446@P10: accuracy labels use a single proxy classification task to keep the conversion path uniform across a
L447@P10: heterogeneous zoo. In addition, the INT8 PTQ path uses a synthetic random-noise representative set for
L448@P10: calibration rather than task-matched real samples, which can under-represent activation statistics for
L449@P10: some architectures and contributes to the observed long-tail accuracy drops. Finally, NNAPI behaviour
L450@P10: is runtime-dependent: the Kirin 710 “NPU” column is a CPU fallback and is flagged as such in every
L451@P10: affected record.
L452@P10: 10. Conclusion
L453@P10: AI on the Edge shows that large-scale, real-device, delegate-resolved benchmarking need not be
L454@P10: expensive. An automated two-stage pipeline with a reconnection guardian, thermal management,
L455@P10: and a resumable ledger measured 586 diverse architectures across five phones — 5,826 delegateresolved records — in roughly 56 unattended device-hours, at up to 201 models/h/phone. We
L456@P10: release the pipeline, the per-run dataset with a documented schema, and a reproducibility harness,
L457@P10: providing a reusable substrate for hardware-aware architecture research, latency-predictor training,
L458@P10: and quantization studies.
